System Map

Read together, the five themes share one pool of workers. Five loops connect them. Pay draws people into work (B1): competition for scarce staff slowly brings people at home into jobs. Deadline forces conversion (B2): the end of temporary protection pushes Ukrainians onto ordinary permits. Fewer workers, more unmet care (R1): care short of staff leaves families to care unpaid. Shortages push caps up (B3): capped sectors press for higher limits. Budgets cap care hiring (B4): wage bills outrun care budgets. Arrows that cross a colour are connections no single theme carries.

LoopNameWhat it doesThis cycle
B1Pay draws people into work
US workforce		Slower labour-supply growth means more hiring from other employers, competition bids up pay, and higher pay draws people at home into work.Turning: participation at a record high
B2Deadline forces conversion
Ukrainians in Europe		The more people hold protection that is about to end, the more pressure to open routes into ordinary permits, and each conversion lowers the number at risk.Priming: uptake still low
R1Fewer workers, more unmet care
Health and care		Slower labour-supply growth leaves care short of staff, unmet care pulls family members out of paid work, and that slows labour supply further.Priming: care's feeders narrowing
B3Shortages push caps up
Asian caps		Tighter caps leave capped sectors short of workers, and the shortages build pressure to raise or review the caps.Priming: reviews asked, none raised
B4Budgets cap care hiring
Health and care		More care hiring raises care wage bills, and strained budgets then limit how many staff can be paid for.Priming: wages up, fees not

Hover over a status for its meaning: Turning means every step in the loop has current evidence, so it is running now. Priming means the parts are in place but the circle has not yet closed at scale.

The Scenario Matrix’s horizontal axis asks whether foreign workers are rationed or admitted on demand, which is whether loop B3 (shortages push caps up) ever releases the caps; its vertical axis asks whether people at home are drawn into work, which is whether loops B1 (pay draws people into work) and B2 (deadline forces conversion) deliver.

What it means: the link that ties the five themes together is that every source of new workers now runs through people already present: those drawn in by pay, those converted from temporary status, and those kept longer under caps. The levers an organisation controls are whom it keeps, whom it helps convert, how it plans around care, and which countries and routes it relies on.
